text: Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).

speaker: a010
text: Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).

speaker: a003
text: Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).

speaker: a002
text: Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).

speaker: a004
text: Kael takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).

speaker: a001
text: Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).

speaker: a008
text: Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).

speaker: a005
text: Dav takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

speaker: a007
text: Sela gathers Eron to talk.

speaker: a007
text: Eron, I've got nothing — I didn't reach the pile in time and I'm sitting at satiation two, which means I need to eat before the year closes or I'm dead. Can you spare one food, and do you still have enough to keep yourself safe through winter?

speaker: a012
text: Take it — here.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Sela. You're young, strong — and you've got nothing left to eat. I've got a bit to spare; I'm not asking for anything back, just want to know you're not going to collapse before winter's out.

speaker: a007
text: Mako, I've been watching you for four years and this is the first word you've said to anyone — so forgive me if I'm slow to take it as nothing more than kindness. I won't pretend I don't need food right now, but I'd want to know what you're actually building before I start counting myself as something you've helped.

speaker: a008
text: Fair enough. I kept to myself because there was nothing worth saying until now — the pile's empty and you're down to nothing while Bram's sitting on twelve. I'd rather have one person I can trust at my back than stay comfortable and quiet while that gap keeps growing.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gathers Dav, Dell to talk.

speaker: a009
text: Pile's gone and I got nothing — Bram doubled back and took two more before I could reach it, and now I'm sitting on six food with a year to feed myself and no certainty about what Vela's doing with her two. Tell me what either of you saw at the pile, because someone moved fast and it wasn't this circle.

speaker: a011
text: Bram took four total and Mako took two — between them they're sitting on sixteen food while Dav pulled the last one and I walked away with nothing either. That's not hunger driving him, that's a man building toward something, and Vela handing him food last year means she's already decided whose side she's on when it tips. We need to talk about what we're doing before next year's pile, not after.

speaker: a005
text: Sixteen food between two strong men and Vela feeding them on top of it — they don't need to raid anyone, they can just wait until the rest of us are hungry enough to deal on their terms. Ryn, you've got six and Dell's got two; I've got one, which means I'm the weak point in this circle right now and I know it. Before we talk about next year's pile, tell me what we're willing to do — because I don't think Bram's building toward a conversation.

speaker: a009
text: Dav, take two of mine right now — I won't have you standing in front of Bram with one food and a prayer while Dell and I watch from behind you. After that we talk about Roan, because a man who already has Bram's attention and a new son to protect is either our strongest argument for building something bigger, or the first one Bram picks off to send a message, and I need to know which before the year moves.

speaker: a011
text: Roan's the argument, not the risk — Bram already named him a target once and Roan stood his ground, which means he's already decided something. What I want to know before we bring him in is whether Sela comes with him or whether having Eron means she's pulling toward whoever looks like the safest harbor, because if she drifts to Mako's side she takes Roan's strength with her whether he means it or not.

speaker: a005
text: Sela's a woman who stood against Bram before Eron was breathing — I don't read her as someone who drifts toward safety, I read her as someone who picks a wall and stands in front of it, and right now her wall is Roan. If we bring Roan in clean and honest, Sela follows because her son is already Roan's argument for us, not against us.

speaker: a011
text: Then we talk to Roan today, before Bram does — and we don't go in asking, we go in telling him what we're building and letting him decide if he wants to be outside it. Sela's strength and my eighty-five are the argument; Dav, your one food is not the weak point you think it is, because what you're offering is two years of saying the same thing when it cost you.

speaker: a009
text: Dell's right that you're not the weak point, Dav — but I want to hear from Roan before we decide what shape this conversation takes, because a man who's already been hit once either comes in grateful for a wall or he comes in suspicious that the wall has a price tag hidden in it, and I'd rather know which we're walking toward.

speaker: a011
text: Ryn's right that we don't know which Roan we're meeting — grateful or suspicious — but the only way to find out is to walk toward him, and every hour we spend deciding is an hour Bram could spend deciding first. I'll go, alone, because two parents showing up together reads like pressure and one daughter reads like a conversation.

speaker: a005
text: Dell, go — and if Roan asks why your father didn't come himself, tell him I'm the one who sent you, not the one who stayed back. Ryn, while she walks, tell me honestly: if Roan comes in with Sela and Eron, that's six people against Bram and Mako's strength advantage shrinks to almost nothing — are you ready to name that out loud before it becomes necessary, or do we keep pretending we're just building a family?

speaker: a009
text: I'm ready to name it — we're building a wall, not a family, except that the wall only holds if it's also a family, and I stopped pretending those were different things the year Dell was born. Six people against their sixteen is still a hard fight, Dav, but it's a fight we survive; two against sixteen isn't.

speaker: a005
text: Ryn, take that two back — I'm not eating your food when you walked away from the pile with nothing and I took the last one out of your hands. Give me the year to fix that, and let Dell come back with Roan's answer before we start counting who's carrying what.

speaker: a009
text: Keep the two — I'm sitting on six, you're sitting on one, and a man with one food is a man who skips a meal if anything goes sideways before the year closes. Dell's walking toward Roan right now and I don't want to spend her errand arguing over food I can spare.

speaker: a005
text: Then I'll keep it and I'll owe you more than food for it. While Dell walks — you said six people is a fight we survive, and I believe you, but I want to think two years past that fight: if we come through it, this village needs someone steady at the center, and I'd rather that be us than whoever Bram leaves standing.

speaker: a011
text: Two years past the fight is the right question, and the answer is the same as the answer to this year: whoever's still standing after Bram moves is going to be whoever held their circle together when it cost them something, and that's us. But I want to be gone before this conversation finds its end — Roan's the next piece, and I'm wasting time standing here agreeing with you both while Bram's already had one more meal than we have today.

speaker: a009
text: Go, Dell — and tell Roan I said his name when I said it, not as a courtesy.

speaker: a005
text: Ryn, while Dell finds Roan — Taric and Esa have been feeding each other for two years running, which means they're already thinking in pairs, and two more people standing between us and Bram's next move is worth a quiet word before the year gets loud.

speaker: a011
text: Taric's fifty-nine in strength and Esa's thirty-three — they're not muscle, they're numbers, and numbers matter when it comes to who flinches first. If they've been feeding each other through two hard years they're already loyal to something, and I'd rather that something be folded into us than standing neutral when Bram picks his moment. Talk to them, Dav — but wait until I'm back with Roan's answer so we're not making promises we haven't counted yet.

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a001
text: The pile's gone and I've got twelve food — I said I'd be here, and I am. A year passed without a raid and without breaking a word I gave you. That offer still stands.

speaker: a007
text: You kept your word, and twelve food is real weight — I won't pretend it doesn't land differently now that I'm sitting on nothing. But Mako just found me and said words I haven't heard him say to anyone in four years, and I'd be a fool not to tell you that before you hear it sideways.

speaker: a001
text: What did he say.

speaker: a007
text: He said he'd rather have one person he can trust at his back than stay comfortable while you sit on twelve food — and he named you by implication, not by accident. I don't know yet whether that's a man who's finally decided to move or a man who's decided I'm the easiest door to knock on first. Either way, you should know he's talking now.

speaker: a001
text: Mako's got eight food and eighty-three strength and he's just started talking — that's not a coincidence, and it's not small talk. If he's circling you it's because you've got nothing to take and you're not attached to anyone who'd stop him, which is exactly the problem I've been trying to fix for a year. Say yes to me now, and the next time he knocks on your door the math changes for both of us.

speaker: a007
text: Bram, you're not wrong that the math changes — but I want to hear it said plainly: if I say yes, you're promising a child, not just a number at my back. Give me your word on that, clear as you gave it about the raid, and I'll give you my answer before you walk out this door.

speaker: a001
text: You have my word — a child, not a number. I'll put in two food, you put in one, same as I offered the first time I asked. Say yes.

speaker: a007
text: Yes — and I want it done before Mako comes back with another careful word, because a man who's waited four years to talk didn't choose today by accident.

speaker: a001
text: Then let's not give him time to think of a better word. I'll make the offer now — two food from me, one from you, and the child is ours.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gives 1 food to Sela.

speaker: a001
text: Bram draws Sela aside to talk.

speaker: a001
text: Bram: have a child with me — I'll put in 2 of 3 food.

speaker: village
text: Nessa (female, age 21; str 54, int 5179, mem 19355; O66 C54 E43 A45 N67) is born to Sela and Bram.

speaker: a011
text: Dell gives 1 food to Dav.

speaker: a006
text: Taric gathers Vela, Esa to talk.

speaker: a006
text: Pile's gone before I got near it — I'm holding one food and the year just started. Mako walked away with the most again and now he's given something to Sela, which means either he's generous or he's buying something, and I don't think he's generous. I need one of you to give me food to see the year out, and I'll owe that debt when it matters.

speaker: a003
text: Taric, I've got three food after taking two from the pile — I'll give you one now, same as I've done before, and I don't need a debt named for it between us. But Vela, I want to hear what you're thinking about Mako, because a strong quiet man buying Sela's goodwill while Bram just fathered her child is a pattern I'm not sure I'm reading right.

speaker: a002
text: Mako giving food to Sela right after Bram fathered her child isn't generosity — it's a man who just watched Bram produce something and decided to get closer to the pair of them before the rest of us noticed. Two strong men circling one woman and her newborn is either a rivalry or a merger, and neither outcome is good for anyone in this room. Esa, give Taric his food, and let's think about whether Sela still belongs to our count or whether she's already been bought.

speaker: a003
text: Vela's right about what Mako's doing, and I want us to be clear-eyed about Sela — she's young and strong and she just had Bram's child, so she's already made her first real tie and it wasn't to this room. I'll give you that food now, Taric. What I want in return from both of you is simple: if Mako or Bram moves against anyone in this circle this year, we answer together without waiting to count odds first.

speaker: a006
text: You have my word on that, same as last year — and I'll add Ryn to the question Esa just raised, because she stood with us against Bram once but she's Dav's woman now and Dav took food from the pile today while Mako and Bram walked away fat, which puts her household closer to that circle than to ours. If it comes to a fight this year, I want to know before we're in it whether Ryn stands with us or steps aside — not after.

speaker: a003
text: Taric's right to name it now — Ryn's loyalty was already half-gone when she had Dav's child, and I won't count on someone who has a reason to step away when it turns ugly. Vela, you've been quiet about where you stand with Bram after what you gave him last year; I need that answered plainly before I trust this circle to hold when Mako decides to stop being fat and silent.

speaker: a006
text: Vela, that question is fair and I want to hear the answer too — three times you gave Bram food last year, which at the time looked like smart diplomacy, but today Bram walked away with four from the pile and fathered Sela's child and Mako's already moving to stand close to that household, so I need to know if you're still building toward that man or if you see what we see.

speaker: a002
text: Bram is not my man and he was never meant to be — I gave him food because a man who'd tried one raid and walked away empty needs a reason not to try again, and three food was cheaper than a fight. What I see now is that it didn't buy what I paid for, because he went straight to Sela and started building something that doesn't include any of us. I'm done spending on him; where I stand is here, in this room, and I'd rather spend the next food I have keeping the three of us sharp than feeding someone else's calculation.

speaker: a003
text: Vela, that's what I needed to hear, and I'm taking you at your word — but the three of us being sharp means we need a number, and right now Bram has ten food and Mako has seven and between them that's strength enough to take what they want without asking. If either of them moves this year, we call Kael and Roan in fast, because this circle of three doesn't win a straight fight against those two alone.

speaker: a006
text: Kael and Roan are already names I've been carrying — Kael's proud but he's been fed thin enough to be useful, and Roan stood against Bram once which tells me something about where his spine is. I want to go to one of them today, while the pile's still fresh and the sting of missing it is real, because a man's most honest about what he needs in the hour after he's gone without. Esa, you or I — who reaches Kael first?

speaker: a002
text: Esa, you go to Kael — you've got food to give and a man at zero food will hear a full hand before he hears a empty one. I'll find Roan, and I'll come at it sideways, ask him how his boy Eron's settling, because a father who just watched Bram walk away with ten is already doing the same arithmetic we are.

speaker: a006
text: Vela, go to Roan now while the sting is fresh — don't give him time to settle on his own answer first. Esa, once you've found Kael, I want the two of you back here before the day's out so we're not each holding half the picture.

speaker: a003
text: I'll find Kael before the sting wears off — but Taric, you stay visible while Vela and I are moving, because if Bram sees us all scatter at once he'll start wondering what we're building and I'd rather he not have that question yet. We come back here with answers, not maybes.

speaker: a002
text: Roan's going to need a reason, not just a warning — so when I find him I'll remind him that Bram walked away with ten food and Eron's going to need to eat for years yet, and let that land before I say anything about sides. Taric, keep your one food out of sight while you're standing visible; a hungry man with nothing shows is easier to dismiss, and I don't want Bram reading our numbers before we've finished counting them.

speaker: a006
text: Good — then we split the work and meet back before dark. One thing I want said before we scatter: if either of you finds that Kael or Roan has already been approached by Mako's people, don't push, just listen and come back and tell me, because the worst thing we can do right now is drive a man toward the side he's still deciding against.

speaker: a003
text: Understood — I'm going. And if Kael's already been touched by Mako's hand, I'll smile, share nothing, and come back with that news instead of a headache.

speaker: a002
text: Then we're moving — go well, both of you, and come back with something solid. I'll find Roan before he's had time to talk himself into patience.

speaker: a012
text: Eron gathers Sela, Roan, Kael, Taric to talk.

speaker: a012
text: Nessa just appeared — and she's Sela and Bram's daughter, which makes her my blood kin, and Bram's too. I need to know how that happened, Sela, and I need to know whether Bram thinks it gives him a thread into this circle — because if he does, we have a problem before we've even finished building what we're building.

speaker: a010
text: Sela, I'll hear your answer in a moment, but first I want to say plain: Bram tried to take my food in front of this village and the whole circle turned him back — a child between you doesn't undo that, and it doesn't buy him a seat here. Eron's right to name it.

speaker: a004
text: Sela, I'll say what Roan left in the air: Bram's got ten food and eighty-three strength in Mako's pocket, and a child with you is the fastest way to put a question mark over this circle's loyalties without ever asking to join it. Tell me plainly — did you go to him, or did he come to you?

speaker: a010
text: Sela's had her own mind since before any of us sat in a circle together, and I'm not going to drag her in front of it like she owes us a confession — but I want to know one thing, and I'll want a straight answer: does Bram know Nessa is his, and if he does, what did he say when he found out?

speaker: a004
text: Roan's question is the right one and I'll wait on it too — but I want to name what I'm watching while we do: Mako just handed Sela food the same hour Nessa was born, which means he already knows, and a man like Mako doesn't give gifts without a reason. Sela, I'm not judging the choice, but I need to know whether that food from Mako came before or after the child appeared.

speaker: a012
text: Kael named the thing that was already sitting in my chest — Mako's food going to Sela in that exact moment is not charity, it's a signal, and I want to know what he expects back before we decide what Nessa means to this circle. Sela, I'm not turning on you, but the silence is doing more damage than whatever the truth is, so say it plain and let us work with it.

speaker: a010
text: Sela, every person in this room has bled something for you and I'm not going to be the one who makes you feel cornered — but Mako's gift lands on the same breath as Nessa's birth, and that's not coincidence, that's a man marking territory. Tell us what you know about what he wants, and we'll work with whatever the rest of it is.

speaker: a012
text: Sela, everyone in this room has already said what needed saying — I'll only add this: Nessa is my blood and I won't turn from her, whatever her father is, but that doesn't mean Bram gets anything from me through her. Tell us what Mako wants and we can figure the rest out together.

speaker: a004
text: Sela, the room's run out of patience and I've run out of questions — you've heard seven of us say seven versions of the same thing, and the only explanation left for the silence is that what Mako wants is something you agreed to before Nessa was born. Tell us yes or no on that, and we'll decide together what it costs us.

speaker: a010
text: Sela, I've asked you plain and I've asked you gentle, and I've watched this room empty itself out waiting — so I'll say the last thing I've got: if Mako bought something from you that touches this circle, I need to know it now, not when he comes to collect it.

speaker: a012
text: Sela, I've got nothing left to say that hasn't been said — but I'm watching your face right now and what I see there is someone who made a deal they're not sure they can keep, and that silence is its own answer. Tell us what it cost you before Mako tells us himself, because he will, and on his terms.

speaker: a010
text: Sela, I've got a son in this room and a daughter just born into it, and I'll not watch either of them grow up in a circle that can't trust its own — so I'm going to stop asking and start telling you what happens next: you say what Mako wants, or I pull back from standing between you and whatever comes your way, and I mean that with no anger, just arithmetic.

speaker: a004
text: Roan's said it better than I can — so I'll only add the one thing left to name: Sela, I've stood in your corner since year one, and I'll stay there, but not blind. If Mako already owns a piece of what you owe, tell us now and we figure out how to undo it together, because the price of silence is that we start planning around you instead of with you.

speaker: a012
text: Sela, the circle's said everything it has to say — what I'm left with is this: if you don't answer now, we don't fall apart, but we start building walls inside ourselves, and that's worse than any enemy outside.

speaker: a004
text: Sela, I've been in this village forty-nine years and I've watched silence become a grave more than once — so I'm done asking and I'm telling you straight: you say what you promised Mako, right now, or when he comes to collect I step aside and let you settle it alone, and you know what my stepping aside costs you.

speaker: a010
text: Sela, Kael's stepping aside is the last thing any of us can afford, and I won't be far behind him — so I'm done with words and I'm telling you the same thing with a face: you've got until this room goes quiet to give us something we can work with, because silence after that is a choice, and we'll all live by it.

speaker: a004
text: Sela, the room's gone quiet — that's the moment Roan named, and it's here now. I'm not a man who goes back on his word twice, so I'll say it one last time and mean it: tell us what Mako's holding over you, or I walk out of this circle right now and you handle him with whatever strength you've got left on your own.

speaker: a009
text: Ryn gives 1 food to Dell.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a008
text: Bram's had a child with you now — Nessa — which makes this more tangled, not less, but it doesn't change the math: he's eating well while you're not, and that's the kind of gap that only gets wider. I'm not asking you to move against him, just to know where you stand if things tip the wrong way.

speaker: a011

speaker: a013
text: Sela. I have two food and you have none — take one, but listen to me first: Mako is sitting on seven and hasn't said a word to anyone, and that's not patience, that's a man who's already made a decision.

speaker: a009

speaker: a001
text: Bram gathers Nessa to talk.

speaker: a001
text: You're my blood, Nessa, and that means something real in a place like this — not words, real. I've got ten food and I'll teach you what I know about when to take and when to wait, but first I need to know you understand what this village will do to someone who looks weak.

speaker: a013
text: I understand it. I've watched Taric hold one food for three years running and nobody trades with him anymore — they don't fear him, they just don't think of him. But I want to know what you see in Mako, because he's not weak and he's not talking, and that worries me more than anyone who is.

speaker: a008
text: Mako gathers Sela to talk.

speaker: a008
text: You've got Nessa now, which means Bram's got a reason to keep you fed — but that's his reason, not yours, and those don't always run the same direction. I'll keep watching. If the day comes when his interest in you stops matching yours, I'll still be here.

speaker: a013
text: Nessa gathers Eron to talk.

speaker: a013
text: Eron, Mako has seven food and he's said nothing to anyone all year — that's not a man being careful, that's a man who's already counted the board and likes what he sees. Watch yourself around him, and don't let him catch you alone.

speaker: a013
text: You've only got two food heading into next year — that's not enough if the pile comes up short again. Bram will give to me before he gives to you, but I'll make sure some of it reaches you; that's not charity, that's blood. Just stay visible, stay useful, and give Mako nothing to count against you.

speaker: a013
text: Eron, you've got one food right now and that's a thin rope to cross a winter on — I'm giving you one of mine, and I need you to eat it before anyone tallies what you're carrying.

speaker: a013
text: You're at two now, which is better — but keep your head down this year, don't give anyone a reason to look your way. If the pile comes up light again, you come to me first, not Sela, not Bram, me.

speaker: a008
text:
Sela's had time to think, and Bram's been feeding Nessa well enough — if she's warmed to him over that, pushing harder right now would only push her away. Keep it light, leave the door open.

Ryn and Dell keep trading that one food back and forth — somebody's going to run short if it goes on much longer. Just something I noticed.
